media.title: Amazon Underworld
media.plot: Explores the hidden world beneath the Amazon River, featuring pink river dolphins navigating flooded forests during the wet season.

media.title: River Monsters
media.plot: Jeremy Wade explores the Amazon's aquatic life, encountering the enigmatic pink river dolphin and the myths surrounding it.

media.title: Wildest Latin America: The Amazon
media.plot: Documents the incredible biodiversity of the Amazon basin, including the pink dolphin's remarkable adaptations to freshwater life.

media.title: The Amazon: Soul of a River
media.plot: A cinematic exploration of the Amazon River ecosystem and the species that depend on its seasonal flood pulse, including the boto.

habitat.description: Amazon river dolphins (boto) inhabit the murky waters of the Amazon and Orinoco river basins, navigating flooded forests during the wet season with remarkable echolocation abilities. Unlike ocean dolphins, they have flexible necks that allow them to weave through submerged trees. They are found in main river channels, tributaries, lakes, and seasonally flooded forests (varzea and igapo).

threats.name: Dam Construction
threats.description: Hydroelectric dams fragment river systems, isolating dolphin populations and altering the flood cycles they depend upon for feeding.

threats.name: Mercury Pollution
threats.description: Artisanal gold mining releases mercury into rivers, bioaccumulating through the food chain to toxic levels in top predators like dolphins.

threats.name: Bycatch and Intentional Killing
threats.description: Dolphins are killed for use as fish bait (particularly for piracatinga catfish) and die as bycatch in fishing nets.

threats.name: Deforestation
threats.description: Clearing of riparian and floodplain forests reduces food availability and increases sedimentation in dolphin habitat.

conservationStatus.population: Unknown total; declining significantly in surveyed areas. Some populations have halved in recent decades.
keyPrograms: Brazilian federal protection (2014 ban on piracatinga fishing)

culturalSignificance.overview: Known as the boto or 'pink dolphin,' the Amazon river dolphin occupies a central place in Amazonian folklore. Local legends describe the boto as a shapeshifter that transforms into a handsome man at night to seduce young women at riverbank festivals. This mythology has paradoxically both protected (through fear and respect) and endangered (through persecution) the species.
